questions.question: Under what condition will the magnitude of average velocity be equal to the average speed?

options.text: When the object moves in a circular path.
options.explanation: In a circular path, displacement and distance are not equal.

options.text: When the object changes its direction of motion.
options.explanation: Changing direction affects displacement and distance differently.

options.text: When the object moves along a straight line without changing direction.
options.explanation: In this case, displacement magnitude equals distance, so average velocity magnitude equals average speed.

options.text: When the object is at rest.
options.explanation: At rest, both average velocity and average speed are zero, but this is a trivial case.

questions.explanation: Average velocity is the ratio of total displacement to total time, while average speed is the ratio of total distance to total time. If an object moves along a straight line without changing direction, its displacement magnitude is equal to the distance covered. Hence, average velocity magnitude equals average speed.
questions.hint: Consider the definitions of average velocity and average speed.

questions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a velocity of 30 m/s in 10 seconds. What is the distance traveled by the car during this time?

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation; the correct distance is 150 m.
Correct calculation using the equation of motion.
Duplicate option; same as B.
Incorrect calculation; the correct distance is 150 m.

questions.explanation: Using the equation of motion: s = ut + (1/2)at². Initially, u = 0 m/s. Final velocity, v = 30 m/s. Time, t = 10 s. Acceleration, a = (v - u)/t = (30 - 0)/10 = 3 m/s². Distance, s = 0 + (1/2) × 3 × (10)² = 0 + 150 = 150 m.
questions.hint: Use the equation of motion for uniformly accelerated motion.
